title: E0014: Law of Demeter
plain_english: The Law of Demeter discourages reaching through one object to access another object's internals. In practice, this rule flags method chains that navigate through unrelated objects.
why_matters: Long call chains like `$a->getB()->getC()->doSomething()` tightly couple code to the structure of multiple objects. Small changes in one class can ripple through callers, making code harder to change and test.
what_it_checks: Method chaining that violates the Law of Demeter.
A method should generally call methods on: `$this`, objects created inside the method, objects passed as parameters, or direct properties of the class.
